name: Can the Fourier infrastructure be extended to handle polynomial progressions (Bergelson-Leibman)

knowledge.progressSummary: PARTIAL — tractable carve-out VERIFIED and EXTENDED. Part (a): the Sárközy square-difference Fourier identity sqDiffCount_fourier (SD(A)=N⁻¹·Σ_r‖Â(r)‖²·G(r)) is machine-checked, 0-axiom, in RothTheorem.lean (researcher-5, #35039). Now ALSO machine-checked (researcher-3, 2026-07-07): sqDiffCount_fourier_main — the circle-method principal-term extraction SD(A)=|A|²+N⁻¹·Σ_{r≠0}‖Â(r)‖²·G(r), peeling the r=0 frequency (‖Â(0)‖²·G(0)=|A|²·N) off the identity to expose the |A|² main term plus the nonzero-frequency error the circle method bounds. This was drafted but infra-blocked in #35159; build-verified this session at the default 32GB memory limit (7743 jobs, 0 sorry / 0 axiom) after fixing two real defects in the draft: (1) sqGaussSum's zero literal needed a ZMod N type annotation, and (2) the summand had to be passed explicitly to Finset.sum_eq_add_sum_diff_singleton — leaving it inferred forced a higher-order unification against the full Fourier sum that blew past 50GB. Part (b) — genuine multi-term polynomial progressions {x,x+n,x+n²} (Bergelson-Leibman) — remains open: provably NOT controlled by the linear (U²) transform, requires Gowers U^s norms + PET, absent from Mathlib 4.26. Axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only.
insights: The existing Roth Fourier infrastructure is genuine and 0-axiom: RothTheorem.lean defines fourierCoeff A r = ∑_{x∈A} ψ(r·x) on ZMod N, proves Parseval (∑_r ‖Â(r)‖² = |A|·N), and the key linearization triple_count_fourier: tripleCount(A) + |A| = N⁻¹·∑_r Â(r)²·conj(Â(2r)). The 3-AP count linearizes ONLY because the pattern (x, x+d, x+2d) is a linear form: character orthogonality in x forces the frequency relation and collapses two of the three Fourier factors into Â(r) and Â(2r).

Structural answer to the OQ, part (a) — Sárközy/single square difference IS an accessible extension. For A ⊆ ZMod N the square-difference count SD(A) = ∑_{x,n} 1_A(x)·1_A(x+n²) Fourier-expands (identical orthogonality bookkeeping to triple_count_fourier) to SD(A) = N⁻¹·∑_r |Â(r)|²·G(r), where G(r) = ∑_{n∈ZMod N} ψ(r·n²) is a quadratic GAUSS sum. Principal term r=0: G(0)=N, Â(0)=|A| ⇒ |A|². The new ingredient vs 3-APs is that the non-principal terms are weighted by G(r) (size ≈ √N for r≠0 by classical Gauss-sum bounds) instead of a second coefficient Â(2r). So the LINEAR transform + Weyl/Gauss-sum estimates suffice — this is exactly the circle-method route to Sárközy's theorem.

Structural answer, part (b) — genuine polynomial PROGRESSIONS (Bergelson-Leibman) are NOT linear-Fourier accessible. Patterns with ≥2 nonlinear terms, e.g. {x, x+n, x+n²}, are provably NOT controlled by the U² (linear Fourier) norm: their count sees quadratic phase correlations invisible to Â. The required machinery is higher-order Fourier analysis (Gowers U^s norms, s≥3) plus PET (Polynomial Exhaustion Technique) induction, or the ergodic Bergelson-Leibman theorem via Furstenberg correspondence (see FurstenbergCorrespondence.lean). None of this — Gowers norms, inverse theorems, PET — exists in Mathlib 4.26. So 'extend the [linear] Fourier infrastructure' to the full Bergelson-Leibman setting is a >1000-line foundational program and open as a formalization target.

Depth-1 OQ chain (single -oq- segment) but 0 follow-up questions generated: the natural children (formalize the SD Fourier identity; formalize Gowers U³) are already captured as nextSteps here, and a new gallery OQ entry would just duplicate them.
builtItems: RothTheorem.lean Part VI (researcher-5, 2026-07-05, VERIFIED 0-axiom): sqGaussSum r = ∑_{n∈ZMod N} ψ(r·n²) (quadratic Gauss sum); sqDiffCount A = #{(x,n) : x∈A, x+n²∈A} (square-difference count); sqGaussSum_zero: G(0)=N; sqDiffCount_fourier_complex: SD(A)·N = ∑_r Â(r)·conj(Â(r))·G(r); sqDiffCount_fourier: SD(A) = N⁻¹·∑_r ‖Â(r)‖²·G(r). Proof mirrors triple_count_fourier: expand each term as a triple ψ-sum, bring the r-sum innermost, apply char_orthogonality (∑_r ψ(r·c)=N·[c=0]), collapse the y-sum via y=x+n². #print axioms → [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
nextSteps: Next tractable step: bound the nonzero-frequency error term N⁻¹·Σ_{r≠0}‖Â(r)‖²·G(r) via |G(r)|≲√N (quadratic Gauss sum bound) + Parseval (parseval_nonzero already gives Σ_{r≠0}‖Â(r)‖²=|A|·N-|A|²), which is the remaining analytic input for a full Sárközy square-difference density bound.
DONE (this result): the Sárközy square-difference Fourier identity SD(A)=N⁻¹·∑_r ‖Â(r)‖²·G(r) — machine-checked, 0-axiom, quadratic analog of triple_count_fourier.

Follow-on (still open): bound the r≠0 terms by |G(r)| ≤ √(2N) (classical Gauss-sum bound) to derive a density-increment for square differences (finite Sárközy). Requires quadratic Gauss-sum magnitude estimates not yet wired for general composite N.
Out of reach in Mathlib 4.26 (document, do not attempt): Gowers U^s norms, the inverse theorem, PET induction — required for genuine {x, x+n, x+n²} polynomial progressions (Bergelson-Leibman).
